description: The line plot illustrates the training loss over iterations for six different models: Vanilla, StrmLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64), SepLLM (n=64, H), SepLLM (n=64, H/T), and SepLLM (n=128). The x-axis represents the number of iterations, ranging from 0 to 140,000, with labeled tick marks at intervals of 20,000. The y-axis represents the loss, scaled from 2.4 to 3.4, with labeled tick marks at intervals of 0.1. All models begin with a high loss value near 3.4 at iteration 0. The Vanilla model, represented by a purple line, shows a rapid initial decrease in loss, stabilizing around 2.7 by iteration 20,000 and remaining relatively flat. The StrmLLM (n=64) model, shown in blue, follows a similar trend, with loss decreasing quickly and stabilizing around 2.8. The SepLLM models, represented by orange, green, red, and dark blue lines, all exhibit a sharp initial drop in loss, reaching values between 2.7 and 2.8 by iteration 20,000, and then plateauing with minor fluctuations. The SepLLM (n=128) model, shown in dark blue, appears to have a slightly lower final loss compared to the other SepLLM variants. Overall, all models converge to a stable loss value after approximately 20,000 iterations, with the SepLLM variants showing comparable performance to the Vanilla and StrmLLM models.
